questions.stem: When making a soluble salt from an acid and an insoluble base, why is the excess solid filtered off?

options.text: To remove excess unreacted base and obtain a pure salt solution
To remove the salt from the water

questions.explanation: Excess insoluble base is added to ensure all the acid has reacted. The unreacted excess is then removed by filtration, leaving a pure salt solution in the filtrate. This solution can then be evaporated and crystallised to obtain dry salt crystals.

questions.stem: Why must the titration method be used to make sodium chloride from hydrochloric acid and sodium hydroxide?

options.text: Because sodium hydroxide is soluble, so excess cannot be filtered off
Because hydrochloric acid is too dangerous to use

questions.explanation: Sodium hydroxide is soluble (it is an alkali), so if excess were added, it would remain dissolved in the solution and contaminate the salt. Titration is used to find the exact volumes of acid and alkali needed for complete neutralisation, ensuring a pure product.
